bug_semantics: Bandit's HTTP/1 parser preserved repeated header lines, but its Content-Length framing path selected only one content-length tuple through List.keyfind/3 and silently ignored every other line. A frontend that framed a request using a different duplicate value could forward body bytes that Bandit, using the selected shorter value, left on the keep-alive connection and parsed as a second request, allowing CL.CL request smuggling across frontend-only WAF, ACL, rate-limit, or audit boundaries.
flaw_origin: Commit e5270b1b19e9f3574aa0f87ec76851d66c38c0af first added Content-Length-based request-body framing in lib/bandit/http1_request.ex. It obtained the request length through a new generic get_header/3 helper implemented with List.keyfind(headers, header, 0), so the very first framing implementation consumed one Content-Length without validating that no duplicate line existed. Later refactors moved this same single-value mechanism into lib/bandit/http1/adapter.ex and then lib/bandit/headers.ex; they did not originate it.
ai_marker: absent: the exact e5270b1b19e9f3574aa0f87ec76851d66c38c0af commit object names author Mat Trudel <mat@geeky.net> and committer Mat Trudel <mat@geeky.net>, and its complete message is only 'Add content-length based body reading'; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer/marker.
evidence: The first-party GitHub security advisory https://github.com/mtrudel/bandit/security/advisories/GHSA-c67r-gc9j-2qf7 identifies CVE-2026-39805, affected versions < 1.11.0, patched version 1.11.0, the vulnerable Bandit.Headers.get_content_length/1 path in lib/bandit/headers.ex, introducer e5270b1b19e9f3574aa0f87ec76851d66c38c0af, and fix https://github.com/mtrudel/bandit/commit/f2ca636eb6df385219957e8934e9fc6efa1630d1.

git show e5270b1b19e9f3574aa0f87ec76851d66c38c0af shows that lib/bandit/http1_request.ex began extracting body_size from get_header(headers, "content-length") and added get_header/3 with List.keyfind(headers, header, 0), while also adding size-based body reads governed by that single selected value. git log --all --reverse -S 'case get_header(headers, "content-length")' -- lib places e5270b1b19e9f3574aa0f87ec76851d66c38c0af first; later hits are rewrites/extraction, including 422651d03b6eb5b2fb10d1ace804880389e7132a creating lib/bandit/headers.ex.

Direct-parent tree verification at d5989c8d8a806639c73d4294762192a7aba3c3ac: lib/bandit/http1_request.ex accumulated incoming header tuples but read_req_body/2 unconditionally returned an empty body; it had no request-side Content-Length lookup, no body_size field, and no List.keyfind-based request framing. git grep for content-length or List.keyfind in lib found only unrelated host lookup in lib/bandit/conn_pipeline.ex and response Content-Length generation in lib/bandit/http1_request.ex. Thus the vulnerable request-framing lines are absent from the immediate parent.

At vulnerable fix parent 21612c7c7b1ce43eccd36d3af3a2299d23513667, lib/bandit/headers.ex:9-14 defines get_header/2 with List.keyfind, and lines 49-56 has get_content_length/1 call that helper once. lib/bandit/http1/socket.ex:55-74 uses that selected length for request framing; lines 131-152 preserve and restore header wire order, so the first duplicate is selected and the other is ignored.

Version-boundary checks resolved tags 0.1.0=4c80fc838640c4dae4743a61494981c57d6eef00, 1.10.4=dea432ec1ec94eee4b9ad0219b09a568c4ccb960, and 1.11.0=e62619895d0d2584d7ffa57d43ef6f72437dfaff. git merge-base --is-ancestor proves the BIC is an ancestor of both 0.1.0 and 1.10.4, matching introduction before the first release. The 1.10.4 lib/bandit/headers.ex tree still uses single-value get_header/2. The fix is an ancestor of 1.11.0, whose tree instead filters all content-length tuples and rejects the multiple-header case.

git show f2ca636eb6df385219957e8934e9fc6efa1630d1 shows a one-parent direct source fix over 21612c7c7b1ce43eccd36d3af3a2299d23513667: lib/bandit/headers.ex replaces the single get_header lookup with Enum.filter over every content-length line and returns an RFC 9112 error for multiplicity; test/bandit/http1/protocol_test.exs adds a 400-response regression case for separate duplicate Content-Length lines, including identical values. Because this commit itself contains the corrective diff and has only one parent, fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are the same full object ID.

git cat-file commit e5270b1b19e9f3574aa0f87ec76851d66c38c0af, inspected only after the BIC was established, shows parent d5989c8d8a806639c73d4294762192a7aba3c3ac, human author and committer Mat Trudel <mat@geeky.net>, and no trailers or AI markers. The BIC is an ordinary single-parent commit, so no squash decomposition exists.
reasoning: The vulnerability begins when e5270b1b19e9f3574aa0f87ec76851d66c38c0af makes Content-Length authoritative for request-body framing but obtains it through a helper that returns one matching tuple. The parser already retained all header lines, so a second Content-Length survived parsing yet never participated in framing validation. The immediate parent lacks that request-length selection and size-based framing mechanism, proving parent absence; all later commits found by line and pickaxe history merely rewrite or relocate the mechanism. The BIC predates 0.1.0 and remains present in 1.10.4. Fix f2ca636eb6df385219957e8934e9fc6efa1630d1 directly changes the lookup to inspect the full repeated-header set and reject multiplicity, and it is contained in patched tag 1.11.0. Finally, the exact BIC commit object contains only Mat Trudel's human author/committer identities and a plain message with no AI attribution, so the vulnerability has a proven human BIC and the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
